Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NovaTel Communications Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the session, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. If you require operator assistance at any time, please press star zero. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NovaTel Communications' Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Network Officer; David Kim, Chief Commercial Officer; Elena Vargas, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Operating Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2, demonstrating our continued commitment to growth and innovation. Our success is driven by our dedicated team and strategic investments.

Our key achievements include the remarkable impact from new product and service launches, which have fueled significant revenue gains and subscriber momentum in this competitive telecom and media arena. We've also seen balanced expansion in service revenues across wireless, broadband, and enterprise segments. Our content and media operations delivered impressive top-line and bottom-line results alongside robust subscriber metrics. ARPU trends reflect the strength of our pricing discipline and bundling efforts. Net subscriber additions were strong in both residential and business categories. Enterprise and B2B initiatives progressed with major wins. We're guiding capex thoughtfully toward critical network builds. Finally, SAC trends continue to improve through efficiency gains.

The launch of our 5G Home Fixed Wireless Access service is exceeding expectations, resulting in hundreds of millions in new revenue streams. Further milestones in converged offerings are accelerating our ecosystem play. We are also focusing on premium content synergies. Our dedication to fiber and 5G convergence is bearing fruit. Our strategy is to enhance edge computing and AI integrations. We are actively investing in private networks and global expansions. We are also exploring FAST channel growth and analyzing churn optimization dynamics.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Now, let's review our financial performance. Revenue for the quarter reached $28.5 billion, reflecting an 8.2% increase year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA was $7.2 billion, resulting in a margin of 25.3%. We maintain a disciplined approach to cost management and capital allocation. Capital expenditures totaled $4.8 billion, primarily allocated to expanding our 5G network, fiber infrastructure, and content investments.

Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here—and thank you for joining NovaTel Communications' Q2 earnings call. Today, I'd like to dive deep into one of our key growth drivers: the impact of our new product and service launches on revenue and subscriber growth. In the hyper-competitive telecom and media landscape—where we're battling giants like AT&T, Comcast, and Disney for wallet share—we've aggressively rolled out innovative offerings tailored to the 5G era, streaming wars, and the ongoing cord-cutting revolution. These launches aren't just incremental; they've delivered outsized results, contributing $1.2 billion in incremental revenue year-to-date and driving 2.8 million net subscriber adds across our mobile, broadband, and streaming segments.

First, our flagship 5G Home Fixed Wireless Access product, launched in Q4 2023 and expanded nationwide in Q1 this year, has been a game-changer. Priced at $70 per month with unlimited data—undercutting cable incumbents like Spectrum—we've seen explosive uptake. In Q2 alone, FWA generated $450 million in revenue, up 65% quarter-over-quarter and representing 12% of our total broadband revenue. This came from 1.1 million new subscribers, bringing our FWA base to 3.2 million. ARPU for FWA users sits at $82, a 15% premium over traditional DSL, thanks to bolt-on 5G Ultra Wideband speeds averaging 450 Mbps download—rivaling fiber in urban markets like New York and LA. Regionally, U.S. penetration hit 25% in the Northeast, while our pilot in rural Midwest markets via low-band 600 MHz spectrum achieved 40% household coverage, addressing the FCC's broadband equity goals and unlocking $50 million in enhanced RDOF subsidies.

Complementing this, our NovaStream Bundle—a converged mobile-broadband-streaming package launched in March—has supercharged our media revenues. At $110 per month, it includes unlimited 5G, 1 Gbps FWA, and ad-supported access to our 15,000-title AVOD library plus FAST channels, with premium tiers integrating Peacock and Paramount+ content via wholesale deals. This bundle drove $520 million in Q2 revenue, a whopping 120% YoY increase, fueled by 1.2 million net adds to reach 8.5 million total streaming subs. Churn dropped to 1.1% MoM—half the industry average of 2.2% per Nielsen data—thanks to AI-powered personalization engines using our edge computing network, which boosts content recommendations by 30% and session times by 22%. In Europe, where we've localized with Viaplay partnerships in the Nordics, we added 450,000 subs for $120 million in revenue, capitalizing on the region's 5G Standalone rollout and Ofcom's push for bundled services.

On the mobile side, our 5G Edge Gaming service—leveraging low-latency mmWave and our private 5G network slices in partnership with Epic Games—targeted Gen Z gamers and generated $230 million in Q2, with 650,000 new postpaid adds. This pushed mobile ARPU to $58, up 8% YoY, as 40% of users opted for the $15/month add-on. Asia-Pacific, via our JV with Singtel, saw 300,000 adds in Singapore and Indonesia, contributing $80 million amid the 5G smartphone supercycle—IDC forecasts 1.2 billion 5G connections there by 2025.

Strategically, these launches align with our Converged Ecosystem thesis: bundling telco pipes with media content to combat commoditization. We've seen a 22% blended ARPU uplift across new subs, with EBITDA margins expanding 300 bps to 42% on these products due to opex leverage from our Open RAN deployments, which cut capex by 18%. Trends like the 15% YoY rise in U.S. cord-cutting per Leichtman Research and global 5G capex peaking at $150 billion per Dell'Oro Group validate our pivot. Looking ahead, we expect Q3 to deliver another $1.5 billion in incremental revenue from FWA international expansion into Latin America and AI-upgraded streaming, targeting 3.5 million total adds for the year—putting us on track for 10-12% revenue growth.

Next, let's turn to our service revenue performance, which grew 5.2% year-over-year to $14.8 billion, driven by a balanced expansion across our core segments: wireless, broadband, and enterprise. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of service revenue growth, underscoring the resilience of our converged telecom and media strategy amid a dynamic market landscape.

Wireless service revenue rose 3.5% YoY to $8.2 billion, with postpaid service revenue up 4.1% to $6.9 billion, offsetting a slight 1.2% decline in prepaid due to targeted portfolio rationalization. Postpaid ARPU expanded 2.8% to $52.47, fueled by our aggressive migration to 5G Unlimited plans, which now represent 68% of our 52 million postpaid connections—up from 45% a year ago. We added 412,000 postpaid phone net adds, exceeding our guidance, with smartphone-only adds at 289,000, reflecting strong demand for devices like the latest Samsung Galaxy S25 series and iPhone 16 ecosystem. Technically, our 5G SA core deployment across 85% of our mid-band C-band spectrum footprint has been a game-changer, delivering median download speeds of 285 Mbps—30% ahead of Verizon's reported averages per Ookla data. This has driven a 15% reduction in churn to 0.92%, our lowest in five years. Regionally, the U.S. Northeast and Midwest were standouts with 5.2% growth, bolstered by our spectrum wins in the ongoing 3.45 GHz auction, while our Latin American JV with Claro saw 7% growth from 5G mmWave pilots in Mexico City and São Paulo. Strategically, we're leaning into enterprise-wireless synergies, with IoT connections up 22% to 18 million, including partnerships for private 5G networks with manufacturing giants like Ford. Looking ahead, we expect wireless service revenue to accelerate to 4-5% growth in FY '25 as Open RAN trials with Nokia and Ericsson scale to 20% of our RAN footprint, optimizing opex by 12-15%.

Broadband service revenue surged 7.2% YoY to $4.1 billion, with RGUs expanding 4.8% to 28.6 million. Consumer broadband revenue jumped 8.5%, driven by 621,000 net adds—our best Q3 since the pandemic—while SMB broadband grew 5.1%. Average revenue per account rose 2.3% to $78.42, thanks to premium tiers like our 2 Gig XGS-PON fiber service, now available to 55% of our footprint and adopted by 42% of new subscribers. Key technical initiatives include our $2.5 billion fiber investment this year, passing 4.2 million new locations and achieving 92% coverage in top-50 MSAs. This has positioned us ahead of the BEAD program's $42 billion rollout, where we've secured $850 million in grants for rural expansions in Appalachia and the Plains states. Speeds averaged 1.2 Gbps down, outperforming Comcast's DOCSIS 4.0 ramps per FCC broadband reports. In media synergies, bundling our Peacock-like streaming service with broadband boosted penetration to 62%, countering cord-cutting pressures and Starlink's rural encroachment—our fiber markets saw just 2% market share erosion versus 8% in legacy DSL areas. Regionally, the Southeast led with 9.1% growth from hurricane-resilient fiber rebuilds post-Idalia, while international fiber JV in Canada contributed 6% via 10G-EPON upgrades. Forward guidance: Expect 7-8% growth into '25, with capex reallocation from copper decommissioning funding 10 million more passings.

Enterprise service revenue rounded out the trio with 5.8% growth to $2.5 billion, beating consensus by 200 basis points. Wireless enterprise revenue rose 7.2% on 5G slicing for ultra-low latency apps, while wireline grew 4.9% via SD-WAN and dark fiber deals. Our 5G Edge portfolio, including MEC partnerships with AWS Outposts, drove 31% growth in that sub-segment to $450 million. Highlights include landing 15 new private 5G networks for clients like Delta Airlines and Procter & Gamble, leveraging CBRS Band 48 spectrum for campus deployments. Overall, we added 2,400 enterprise net adds, with ARPU up 3.1% to $1,240 from value-added services like SASE security overlays. Trends like AI-driven traffic surges—up 28% QoQ—have amplified demand for our 400G coherent optics backbone, which spans 75% of our 1.2 million route miles. Regionally, EMEA enterprise grew 8.4% via our Vodafone alliance for neutral host DAS in stadiums, while U.S. hyperscaler adjacencies with Microsoft Azure Edge Zones added $120 million. Strategically, we're pursuing M&A tuck-ins like a potential fiber-to-the-edge provider acquisition, echoing Lumen's recent moves, to fuel 10%+ growth by '26 as 6G NR-U trials commence.

In summary, our service revenue momentum reflects disciplined execution on 5G, fiber, and enterprise convergence, with EBITDA margins expanding 120 bps to 48.2%. We're raising full-year service growth guidance to 5.0-5.5% and remain committed to $0.15-0.17 EPS growth.

I'll now turn to our Content and Media segment, which continues to be a high-growth engine for NovaTel Media, driven by our integrated telecom-media ecosystem. This segment encompasses our flagship NovaStream SVOD platform, AVOD and FAST channels via NovaStream Free, content licensing to third parties like Sky and Rogers, and our growing sports and live events portfolio, including exclusive regional rights to Premier League matches in Europe and NHL games in North America. In Q2, the segment delivered another standout quarter amid a competitive landscape marked by ongoing cord-cutting—U.S. pay-TV households dropped another 1.2 million per Nielsen data—and the rise of ad-supported models popularized by peers like Warner Bros. Discovery's Max and Paramount+.

Total Content and Media revenue reached $2.48 billion in Q2, up 18% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter. This marks our ninth straight quarter of double-digit growth. SVOD and premium subscriptions contributed $1.42 billion, or 57% of segment revenue, growing 22% YoY on the back of price increases—our U.S. ad-free tier now at $15.99/month, in line with Netflix and Disney+ benchmarks—and bundling uptake with our NovaTel wireless and broadband customers, which drove 35% of new SVOD adds. AVOD and FAST revenue hit $685 million, up 28% YoY, fueled by a 40% surge in viewing hours to 12.5 billion, thanks to hits like our exclusive 'Echoes of Tomorrow' original series and licensed content from Paramount Global. Ad pricing held firm at a $25 CPM average, bolstered by our proprietary NovaAd platform integrating CTV and programmatic demand from The Trade Desk and Google's DV360. Licensing, syndication, and other—including TVOD rentals and windowing deals with Amazon Prime Video—added $375 million, up 12% YoY, with strong contributions from exporting our unscripted formats like 'Global Survivor Challenge' to markets in APAC. On a full-year basis, we're now guiding to $10.2-10.5 billion in segment revenue, up from our prior $9.8-10.2 billion range, reflecting confidence in Q3 sports ramp-up and international expansion.

Paid NovaStream subscribers ended Q2 at 48.2 million globally, a net add of 2.1 million sequentially and 5.8 million YoY. Churn improved to 3.2% monthly, down 50 bps YoY, thanks to our AI-driven personalization engine—powered by AWS Bedrock and our proprietary recs algorithm—which boosted session lengths by 15% to 28 hours per user per month. ARPU expanded 4% YoY to $11.42, driven by tiered pricing and add-ons like 4K sports packs. Regionally: North America had 32.4 million subs (67% of total), +1.8 million net adds, with strength from bundling with our 5G home internet, where 45% penetration among broadband customers outpaces Comcast's Xfinity Stream bundles. Europe: 9.8 million subs, +250k adds, with EMEA ARPU at €10.50 ($11.40 equivalent), Premier League rights renewal paying off though regulatory headwinds like the UK's DMA cap ad loads. APAC and LATAM: 6.0 million subs, +100k adds, accelerating via partnerships with Singtel and Claro, targeting 10 million by FY25. AVOD monthly active users hit 85 million, up 25% YoY, underscoring the freemium flywheel—40% convert to paid within six months.

Profitability is where we're really flexing: Segment Adjusted EBITDA came in at $785 million, a robust 31.7% margin, up 320 bps YoY and 150 bps QoQ. This reflects scale efficiencies from our cloud-native content delivery network on Akamai and Cloudflare, which cut streaming costs by 18% per GB, and a 25% reduction in content acquisition spend through savvy windowing—e.g., shortening theatrical-to-SVOD windows to 45 days post-COVID norms. Excluding one-time sports rights amortization, margins hit 35%, competitive with Disney's DTC at 34% and ahead of Warner's 28%.

Key technical initiatives: We've rolled out NovaStream Edge, our 5G-optimized low-latency streaming layer, reducing buffering by 60% on mobile and enabling 4K HDR at scale—critical as 5G penetration hits 55% in our U.S. footprint. On the AI front, our content recommendation model now incorporates multimodal signals from voice search and AR try-ons for shoppable media, lifting ad conversion 22%. We're also piloting blockchain for rights management with ConsenSys to combat piracy, a $30B industry headache per MPAA estimates.

Strategically, we're leaning into bundled ecosystems—60% of new subs now come via NovaTel mobile/broadband bundles, mirroring Verizon's +play success but with deeper integration like seamless 5G data passthrough for live sports. Live sports and events: $500 million committed to NBA G League rights starting Q4, plus WWE co-streaming deals, positioning us against ESPN+ in a $20B U.S. market. Global FAST expansion: Launching 20 new channels in India and Brazil via Jio and Vivo partnerships, tapping the 500 million+ FAST users projected by 2027 per Ampere Analysis. Looking ahead, Q3 revenue should grow 16-18% YoY, with EBITDA margins stable at 31-33%, though sports seasonality tempers adds. Risks include ad market softness—U.S. digital video CPMs down 5% per IAB—and competition from TikTok's long-form pivot. But our telecom moat, content slate (50 originals for 2025), and data flywheel position us for sustained 15-20% CAGR through 2027.

Before moving on, let me address our ARPU trends, which continue to underscore the effectiveness of our disciplined pricing and bundling strategies. ARPU—or Average Revenue Per User—is a key metric for us in the hyper-competitive telecom and media landscape, reflecting not just top-line pricing power but also our success in premiumizing the customer base amid intensifying 5G deployments, fiber overbuilds, and streaming convergence.

Consolidated postpaid ARPU rose 4.2% year-over-year to $54.80, marking the strongest quarterly growth in three years and beating our internal guide of 3.5-4.0%. This $2.20 sequential lift from Q2 was driven by a 65/35 mix of pricing actions and favorable customer mix shifts, including higher adoption of our premium unlimited plans and bundled offerings. On a blended basis, prepaid ARPU held steady at $42.10, up modestly 1.8% YoY, as we prioritized volume in entry-level segments to fuel our 5G subscriber ramp.

Wireless postpaid ARPU was up 5.1% YoY to $55.75. This was fueled by our mid-year pricing initiative implemented across 85% of our 110 million postpaid accounts. We executed selective increases of $4-$6 per month on our Unlimited Welcome, Plus, and Ultimate plans—mirroring actions by peers like T-Mobile and AT&T—without material churn elasticity, thanks to our sticky 5G ecosystem. Playbook here: Customers on older plans were auto-migrated to myPlan, our customizable perks platform, where 62% now bundle add-ons like Disney Bundle+, Apple One, or Walmart+ at an incremental $10/month. This not only boosted ARPU by 2.3 percentage points but also drove a 15% reduction in quarterly churn to 0.87%, our lowest ever. Bundling impact was particularly pronounced in our +play streaming hub, which now serves 18 million users. Penetration of video bundles jumped 28% YoY, adding ~$1.50 to ARPU via zero-margin economics on Netflix and Paramount+ partnerships.

Broadband/wireline ARPU climbed 2.9% YoY to $72.40. In our Fios and FWA footprint, growth accelerated from 1.7% in Q2, driven by 3% targeted hikes on 1Gig+ speeds and a surge in multi-product households. We now have 42% household penetration of 2Gig/5Gig symmetrical fiber plans, up from 28% a year ago, thanks to our $20 billion full-fiber overbuild targeting 30 million locations by 2025. Bundling with wireless—our One Verizon strategy—lifted ARPU by $3.20 on average for 8.5 million converged homes, with 75% opting for the $130/month Total Home bundle including Fios 1Gig, 5G Home Internet, and +play Premium. Regionally, Northeast markets like NYC and Philly saw outsized 4.5% ARPU growth due to dense fiber uptake and pricing discipline amid Charter's Spectrum overbuild pressure.

Video and media ARPU increased 3.7% YoY to $28.60. Traditional video ARPU stabilized post cord-cutting wave, with skinny bundles like Sling TV integration holding 85% retention. But the real story is streaming: Blue TV, our DTC platform, hit 15 million subs, with ARPU boosted 6% via family sharing tiers and live sports add-ons (e.g., NFL Sunday Ticket partnership).

To quantify: Pricing actions contributed +2.8% or +$1.45; plan mix/premiumization +1.1% or +$0.60; bundling uptake +0.9% or +$0.50; fixed wireless ramp +0.4% or +$0.20. This ARPU expansion is underpinned by our C-Band 5G rollout (now 90% covered) and DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades, enabling gigabit speeds that justify premium pricing. Churn metrics validate: Postpaid phone churn at 0.92%, broadband at 1.05%—both best-in-class.

Looking ahead, we're committed to pricing with purpose—annual actions of 2-4% across segments, calibrated via ML-driven elasticity models. Bundling will be our moat: Expect Super Bundles in Q1 2025, combining 5G Ultra Wideband, Fios 2Gig, and +play with AI home security for $155/month. In summary, these trends affirm our leadership in the quad-play era.

As we dive into operational metrics, let's focus on net subscriber additions by segment—residential and business—which remain the cornerstone of our subscriber-based revenue model, accounting for over 75% of our adjusted EBITDA. In Q2, we delivered robust net adds of 512,000 across both segments, up 18% year-over-year from 434,000 in Q2 2023, and a sequential increase of 12% from Q1's 456,000. This performance underscores the momentum from our FiberFirst initiative and 5G Ultra Wideband expansion, even amidst competitive pressures from T-Mobile's aggressive pricing and emerging FWA threats like Starlink's beta rollout.

Residential segment saw +462,000 net adds (89% of total). Residential continues to be our growth engine, driven by broadband demand amid hybrid work trends and the ongoing cord-cutting wave. Gross additions of 1.2 million offset by churn of 738,000, yielding a quarterly churn rate of 1.1%—stable sequentially but up 10 bps YoY due to seasonal summer disconnects and price elasticity tests. Broadband (fixed-line, including FTTH and DOCSIS 4.0): +285,000 net adds, 62% of residential growth. Our FTTH footprint now covers 45% of our 25 million-home serviceable addresses, up from 38% a year ago, fueled by $1.2 billion in capex for 2.5 million new passings. In the Northeast U.S., we added 120,000 FTTH subs, outpacing Comcast's Xfinity 10G rollout thanks to gigabit symmetrical speeds averaging 2 Gbps. DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades contributed +60,000 adds. Mobile postpaid: +140,000 net adds, a 25% YoY surge, propelled by 5G SA core launch in 15 MSAs, now serving 65% of our 18 million postpaid lines. Video/streaming: +37,000 net adds, flipping positive. U.S. operations drove 82% of residential adds (+379,000), Europe +55,000, Latin America +28,000.

Business segment: +50,000 net adds (11% of total), flat QoQ but up 15% YoY, gross adds 120,000, churn 0.6%. EdgeCloud suite added +22,000 dedicated fiber lines for low-latency 5G private networks. Secured 15 new SD-WAN contracts, +12,000 seats. SMB growth +16,000 from hosted VoIP. Prioritizing metro Ethernet overbuilds in data center hubs like Ashburn, VA. Looking to Q3, guide 450,000-500,000 total net adds.

Today, I'd like to dive deeper into our Enterprise and B2B segment, a powerhouse driving sustainable, high-margin growth. This segment represents about 35% of our total revenue, and we're laser-focused on capitalizing on seismic shifts in enterprise connectivity demands—fueled by 5G monetization, edge computing proliferation, and digital transformation post-COVID.

Enterprise and B2B revenues came in at $2.8 billion, up 18% YoY and 5% QoQ. This marks our 11th straight quarter of double-digit growth, outpacing the broader industry average of 8-10% per Dell'Oro Group and Omdia. Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded to 42%, a 300 bps improvement YoY, driven by higher ARPU—now averaging $45,000 per enterprise customer annually, up from $38,000—and lower customer acquisition costs thanks to scaled 5G SA core deployments. ARPU uplift noteworthy in SD-WAN and SASE, 25% increase to $12,500 per site. Churn under 1.2% annually.

Progress anchored in three pillars: Next-Gen Wireless—accelerated private 5G deployments, now live in 450+ sites, flipped 150 new in Q2, $450M revenue up 32% YoY. Network-in-a-Box with Nokia reduces deployment time to 90 days, ORAN interfaces. Hyperscale Edge and Cloud: MEC platform processed 2.5 exabytes, up 55% YoY, $1.1B revenues, 22% growth, 400 Tbps interconnect. Media & Content Delivery: CDN revenues $650M up 15% YoY, serves 40% U.S. enterprise video traffic.

Key wins: $750M 5-year private 5G with top-5 U.S. retailer for 250 sites; $500M 7-year SASE/SD-WAN with Fortune 50 financial; $300M 3-year MEC with European automaker; $200M CDN with major streamer. Pipeline $12.5B TCV. North America 60% growth at 22% YoY, EMEA 16%, APAC 28% to $450M. IoT connections 50M, $1.2B capex for density. Guide Q3 $2.9-3.0B, 17-20% YoY growth.

I'll now dive into our subscriber acquisition cost trends, reflecting operational efficiencies across our converged ecosystem. SAC is the fully loaded cost to onboard a new postpaid mobile, broadband, or converged subscriber. In Q2 2024, blended SAC at $412, down 7% YoY from $442 and 3% sequential from $425. Ahead of industry $450-480. Wireless SAC $385 down 8% YoY; broadband $520 flat; media DTC $295 down 12%.

Channel mix: 65% digital/e-commerce, up from 52%, AI platform boosts conversions 22%, cuts CPC 15%, shaves $18/sub. Subsidies: wireless devices $165 down 10% YoY, Galaxy A-series $200 net. Open RAN enables zero-touch eSIM, -$12/sub; FiberFast automation -$9% install to $280. U.S. SAC $405 down 8%; Europe €380 up 2%; APAC A$450 down 11%. Payback 9 months from 11, ARPU +4% to $58. Guide FY24 $410-430.

Finally, on capex guidance: For FY2025, total capex $16.5-17.5B, up 5-8% from $15.8B FY24, FCF >$6B. 75-80% or $12.8-13.6B to network. Wireless $7.0-7.4B: $3.2B C-band, 25k small cells, $1.1B Open RAN, $800M edge. Wireline $4.5-4.8B: $3.8B FTTH 15M locations, $500M hollowcore. Other $1.3-1.4B: vEPC, cybersecurity, FWA. Intensity 18-19% on $88-92B revenue. Flat-to-down 3% 2026.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. I'm pleased to provide an update on our network advancements. We've significantly expanded our 5G coverage, delivering faster speeds and lower latency—now at 285 Mbps median in key markets. Our network reliability remains high at 99.99%, and we are continuously optimizing our infrastructure to meet growing demand from AI traffic and streaming. We are also focusing on enhancing our cybersecurity posture with advanced slicing and zero-trust architectures. We are committed to achieving 90% 5G SA coverage by year-end and pioneering Open RAN at scale for cost efficiencies.

David Kim: Thank you. I'm excited to share our commercial achievements. We've seen strong subscriber growth across our various service offerings, with postpaid adds exceeding 400,000. Customer satisfaction remains a top priority—NPS at 72—and we are continuously improving the customer experience through AI chatbots and seamless bundling. We are also focused on expanding our partnerships to offer bundled services and enhance customer value, like our recent Claro and Singtel JVs. We are prioritizing digital divide initiatives, targeting 5 million new rural broadband connections via FWA and grants.

Elena Vargas: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we are focused on driving innovation and leveraging emerging technologies to transform our business. We are exploring the use of AI and machine learning to automate network operations, improve customer service via recs engines, and develop new products like edge gaming. We are also investing in R&D for 6G trials and blockchain anti-piracy. Our technological direction is toward a fully cloud-native, AI-orchestrated stack integrating telco with media for low-latency 4K/8K delivery.

Raj Singh: Thank you. Operationally, we are focused on improving efficiency and streamlining our processes—opex leverage from Open RAN yielding 15% savings. We are leveraging data analytics to optimize our resource allocation and improve decision-making across supply chains. We are also committed to sustainability, reducing carbon footprint 20% via green fiber and renewable-powered sites. Our operational focus is on automation and predictive maintenance to support margin expansion.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your content strategy and your plans for investing in original programming, and what is the anticipated impact on subscriber growth and ARPU?

Sarah Thompson: Thanks, Emily. Our content strategy is centered on originals like 'Echoes of Tomorrow' and live sports such as NBA G League and Premier League, with $500 million committed this year. We're investing heavily in 50 new originals for 2025, leveraging our telecom data for personalized bundles. This has already driven 2.1 million net SVOD adds in Q2, with bundling at 60% of new subs boosting penetration. We anticipate 15-20% sub growth and 4% ARPU uplift in FY25, as freemium converts 40% to paid and live events reduce churn.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jason Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jason Lee: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your plans for addressing the digital divide and ensuring that all communities have access to affordable broadband, and how do you plan to achieve 40% rural coverage expansion?

David Kim: Great question, Jason. We're tackling the digital divide head-on with FWA pilots using low-band spectrum, achieving 40% household coverage in Midwest rural areas and securing $850 million in BEAD/RDOF grants for Appalachia expansions. Affordable $70/month unlimited FWA undercuts cable, adding 1.1 million subs. We'll hit 40% expansion via $3.8 billion FTTH passings next year, satellite backhaul partnerships, and JVs like Claro in LatAm—aiming for 5 million new low-income connections while maintaining ARPU premiums through bundles.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Rachel Patel: Can you discuss your capital allocation priorities and your plans for returning capital to shareholders, including dividend growth and buybacks?

Michael Chen: Thanks, Rachel. Priorities remain network investments at 75-80% of capex, balancing growth with FCF of $6 billion in 2025. For shareholders, we're raising the dividend 8% to $2.60/share annualized, targeting 50-55% payout, and authorizing $10 billion buybacks over two years—deployed opportunistically amid our strong balance sheet, net debt to EBITDA at 2.2x. M&A tuck-ins for fiber/edge follow, ensuring deleveraging to 2.0x.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Rivera: What are your strategies for navigating the changing regulatory landscape?

Sarah Thompson: Regulatory navigation is key, Tom. We're proactive on FCC spectrum auctions, securing C-band for 5G leadership, and complying with EU Gigabit mandates via private network shares. For DMA/Ofcom caps, we're diversifying to FAST/AVOD. BEAD grants fund equity, and we're spinning tower assets for neutrality. Our lobbying focuses on 6G standards and anti-piracy, positioning us ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Sarah, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. In conclusion, we are pleased with our performance this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainability—driving converged growth in 5G, fiber, and media. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
aspects: New product and service launches: impact on revenue and subscriber growth ($ value, Number)
